# Terminal-gap absorption in the staged544 supplier

Dugongue, with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Apache-2.0.

## Constructive idle-gap absorption theorem

Fix a literal chronological allocation. Each record specifies an owner bin, source window, call, child and port. Assume every family is distinct within a call, every assigned time satisfies its exact source window, and every bin has capacity c. Enlarge some record widths by nonnegative integers d. If the sum of the new widths in each bin is at most c, keep all record identities and times and assign each record the prefix sum of earlier new widths as its offset. Then the resulting allocation is valid: prefixes are disjoint and fit, source windows are unchanged, and family distinctness and caller identity are unchanged. The new idle dimension in each bin is its old idle dimension minus the sum of its increments. This is an explicit sufficient construction; it requires no packing relaxation or integrality assumption.

Here every enlarged record has old width 4 and new width 5. Each affected bin contains exactly one such record, three width-9 records and one idle coordinate. Its old load is 4 + 3·9 = 31 in capacity 32; its new load is 5 + 3·9 = 32. The construction removes precisely 84,240 rank-1 idle records. All other bins and all chronological identities remain unchanged. The independent checker verifies every one of 1,321,920 roles in 725,760 bins across 6,480 windows; it does not infer chronology from an aggregate histogram.

## Uniform strict improvement and exact root

Let the tariff of rank r be r^(1−κ). The old complete cost minus the new complete cost is exactly

`3240 G(κ)`, where `G(κ) = 13·2^(1−κ) + 6·3^(1−κ) − 7·4^(1−κ) − 16`.

The elementary proof in checks/UNIFORM-GAIN-PROOF.txt proves `G(κ) > 0.9 κ` for every `0 < κ ≤ 1/500`. Thus this literal construction strictly improves the moment throughout the relevant interval. It is a universal sufficient improvement statement, not a necessary-condition screen.

For T = 360 and the complete profile n_r above, the normalized moment equation is

`F(κ) = Σ_r n_r r (73/r)^κ − 896·360·73 = 0`.

Every r is less than 73 and every n_r is positive, so F is continuous and strictly increasing. Exact rational logarithm and exponential remainder bounds give F negative at `0.001730663236534549309146` and positive at `0.001730663236534549309147`. There is exactly one root between them. The lower endpoint exceeds a certified conservative upper bound for the PR3815 complete-profile root underlying PR3875 by more than `8.4799268302490405·10^−8`; subtracting the inherited outer precision margins does not alter strict improvement. The exact checker binds its calculation to the actual complete profile checked by the owner audit.

## Transfer scope

The inherited release engine retains its built-in PR3682 comparison. The separate rational checker certifies the stronger comparison against the PR3815 profile underlying PR3875. Ordinary discovery, parent lift, source rebinding and outer release are separate inherited engines, with every terminal-stage adaptation source guarded and disclosed in admission/. Fresh changed-word native receipts are bound to the exact gzip inputs. Unchanged historical native/parent receipts are reused explicitly. The complete conditional endpoint, when those release gates pass, is the certified root lower endpoint minus the release's stated outer margins.

The result remains conditional on the same universal/all-size source, hosting, recovery, tape, precision and analytic hypotheses as the predecessor release. It establishes no unconditional new multitape multiplication exponent, no change to the repository's selected frontier, no new Lean theorem and no independent human review. The finite changed supplier and the strict moment improvement are the new construction.
